summary: The Swiss Federal Criminal Court convicted former HSBC IT employee Hervé Falciani in his absence of aggravated economic espionage over the leaked client data ('HSBC files') and sentenced him to five years; he was acquitted of the other charges and lived in France, out of reach of extradition. No reward.

target: Bank Julius Bär & Co. AG / Julius Baer Bank & Trust Company Ltd. (Cayman Islands)
summary: Rudolf Elmer, former chief accountant of Julius Bär's Cayman Islands subsidiary, was prosecuted in Zurich for leaking client data to tax authorities, media and WikiLeaks. Zurich courts convicted him in 2011 and 2015 (suspended day-fines); in 2016 the Zurich High Court acquitted him of bank-secrecy offences but gave him a suspended 14-month sentence for threats and forgery, with 220 days already served in pre-trial detention. The Federal Supreme Court upheld the bank-secrecy acquittal in 2018. No reward.
quote: fällte sie eine Freiheitsstrafe von 14 Monaten, wovon 220 Tage durch Untersuchungshaft erstanden seien.
notes: The judgment is anonymised ('X.'); Elmer went public himself and is named for this ruling by law.ch (che-lawch-elmer-2018). Earlier sentences in the same judgment: 240 day-fines of CHF 30 (2011) and 300 day-fines of CHF 150 (2015), both suspended.
